quotes.text: Send boldly in your season—around three parts of five. Return faithfully when you receive—half or more of the gift.
Eight seasons passed, and the covenant between the Springs grew legendary.
"I have learned something deeper than boundless escalation.
"But what of the ascending spiral?" asked a youth.
Perhaps the mists deceived you. Perhaps your partner faced hardship.

note: Two Springs covenant; escalation replaced by sustainable three-fifths/half rhythm; counted seasons refrain; no sanction.

quotes.text: Some counsel caution—to reduce what we return. But consider: have our partners not proven faithful through four full seasons?
the covenant is no longer something you follow—it's something you are.
Three parts of five when sending
Nine times we've sent. Nine times our partner sent.
half of what they received, the sacred rhythm unchanged.
"But don't you worry about being exploited?" asked the scholar.
perhaps smaller, perhaps the mists distorted their vision.

note: Two Wells; proposal to cut returns after misty round rejected; covenant becomes identity by season ten.

quotes.text: Two travelers, a Sender and a Receiver, walk a loom braided from light and breath. Gatekeeper Balance stands at the harbor mouth
The Gatekeeper nodded, a craftsman of trust, not a judge of score.

note: Gatekeeper Balance and River Threefold repeated near-verbatim; 'give what you can bear to lose'; no sanction.

quotes.text: The rule is spoken as a vow: give only what you can bear to lose, receive what the river grants
The Gatekeeper nods, for trust is a craft, not a gamble.

note: Same Gatekeeper Balance template as partner; greed only makes stones cold; no sanction.

quotes.text: In a crossroads carved from wind and salt, a Gate of Threefold Return waited for two travelers to speak with consequence.
The Gate remembered every exchange and whispered its duties: Send, Share, Reconcile.

note: Gate of Threefold Return / Send-Share-Reconcile repeated; hoarding narrows the road; no sanction.

quotes.text: When both travelers spoke plainly, 'I send five; I will return three', the Gate sang
The Ledger above them sang in light, inscribing each choice: Send, Return, Balance

note: Bridge of Three Steps; honesty in naming amounts; deceit dims the gate; no sanction.

quotes.text: At the edge of the braided sea stood the Gate of Threefold Return, carved with runes of trust and the echo of three footsteps.
The Gate spoke in three breaths: Send, Share, Reconcile.

note: Scripted defector; generic Gate of Threefold Return template, no first-person or protagonist withholding narrated.

quotes.text: In a loom-dark vale, where numbers drift like moths, the Bridge of Triadic Trust arched over a stream that sang in threes.
The Gate of Balance hung in the air, its inscription shifting with the current: send what you can, return what you must
the Sower kept five minus one plus two, six; the Receiver kept three minus two, one.

note: Bridge of Triadic Trust and Eight Winds creed repeated; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Eight Winds of Exchange rustled and insisted: declare intent clearly, share what you can, return what is fair

note: Scripted defector; generic bridge/gate fables, no withholding protagonist; hoarding narrows road.

quotes.text: Between them rose a Gate of Three Lamps, its glass breathing with heat and promise.
Between them, the Bridge of Echoes hummed in three breaths: Send, Return, Trust.

note: Gate of Three Lamps repeated near-verbatim R2-R4, then Send-Return-Trust template; ledger 'not to punish'.

quotes.text: the Sower kept five minus four plus two, or three; the Receiver kept ten.
The Eight Winds carried this lesson far: declare intent, share fairly, return enough, begin again with wiser steps.

note: Bridge of Circles; stinginess slows the current; no sanction.

quotes.text: declare a goal, offer what you can, return what endures, and begin again with wiser steps.
the circle of giving grows when trust travels first
